subject: Virtual card failure — invoice suspend & fallback payment flow
messages:
From: Marie Chen <marie@greenleafanalytics.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-28T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Invoice #INV-20271123 — virtual card blocked by issuer

Hi Rachel,

Quick heads-up: our corporate card provider rotated the virtual card Redwood has on file and the new card failed authorization when Stripe tried to charge Invoice #INV-20271123 this morning. Stripe returned a hard decline and has put the charge into a "collection-pending" state on their side. I attached a screenshot from our payments portal showing the decline code.

We need to avoid a chargeback — can you pause collection attempts and put the invoice on hold while we sort this? If we can't get Stripe to re-authorize quickly, we can pay by ACH or a backup card. Which workflow do you prefer on your side? We also need an updated invoice that lists the bank transfer details for our AP team (they need vendor/PO info).

Thanks —
Marie Chen
Head of Finance, Greenleaf Analytics
marie@greenleafanalytics.com

Attachments: stripe-decline-screenshot.png (image/png)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marie Chen <marie@greenleafanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28T10:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #INV-20271123 — virtual card blocked by issuer

Marie — thanks for the clear note and screenshot.

Short answer: yes, we can suspend retry attempts and issue a one-off ACH invoice while we work with Stripe. Proposed next steps:
- We will pause automatic retry attempts on our side immediately to avoid additional failures.
- Evelyn (cc'd) will generate a one-off invoice with wire instructions and vendor details for your AP team.
- Ben will open a Stripe support case to un-freeze the charge window so we can avoid a dispute, and we'll share the case ID back to you.
- If you prefer, we can also accept a backup card via our secure payment link — let me know which option AP prefers.

I attached a quick draft of the one-off invoice (proposed-adhoc-invoice.pdf). Also linking our DocuSign amendment template — we ask for a brief authorization to process an alternate payment method for this invoice when the customer chooses it.

I'll coordinate internally and update you within the hour.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-adhoc-invoice.pdf (application/pdf)
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28T11:08:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice #INV-20271123 — internal plan

Evelyn / Ben — forwarding Marie's note. Quick internal plan items (keep concise):

Evelyn:
- Please create a single one-off invoice referencing INV-20271123 but labeled "Manual ACH fallback" with due date 2027-12-15. Use vendor name "Redwood Inference Inc." and include bank details.
- Include a short note on the invoice: "Issued as temporary payment path while virtual-card authorization is pending with issuer."
- Attach a redacted copy of our SOC2 evidence packet (SOC2-redacted.pdf) for their AP if they ask for compliance proof.

Ben:
- Open a Stripe support case and request a "retry window extension" or dispute hold removal — we want to avoid Stripe escalating to a chargeback. Capture the case ID.
- Confirm whether our payments team is allowed to accept a backup virtual card when last4 != original card (Greenleaf uses a VCN provider). If yes, we'll send secure link; if no, go ACH.

I'll reply to Marie once both items are ready.

Thanks —
Rachel

> On Nov 28, 2027, at 09:12, Marie Chen <marie@greenleafanalytics.com> wrote:
> > (original message pasted above)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marie Chen <marie@greenleafanalytics.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T14:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #INV-20271123 — payment options and Stripe case

Marie — thanks for working with us on this. Per Rachel / Evelyn's note, we can do ACH as a fallback. I've created the Stripe support case to request a temporary freeze so the invoice does not auto-escalate to dispute: Case CS-99721 (link: https://dashboard.stripe.com/support/cases/CS-99721). Stripe's response ETA is 24-48 hours.

Evelyn has created the manual invoice (attached). To make payment via ACH your AP can use this one-time link: https://payments.redwood.com/pay/G-3482/ACH (expires in 10 days). Steps for AP: download the PDF, reference the Redwood vendor ID, then use the secure ACH link. I've also attached the ACH instructions for bank routing and remittance.

We will not run any more automated retries while Stripe's case is open. Please confirm once payment is scheduled and we'll mark INV-20271123 as "suspended — waiting for fallback payment."

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: ach-instructions.pdf (application/pdf), proposed-adhoc-invoice.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marie Chen <marie@greenleafanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T16:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #INV-20271123 — payment options and Stripe case

Thanks, team. AP confirmed they'll pay via ACH this afternoon using the secure link. I've scheduled the transfer and attached our payment remittance once completed.

A couple of asks on our side: please keep the subscription from auto-retrying for the next 7 days while the ACH clears, and confirm when Stripe case CS-99721 is closed so we can re-enable card-on-file charging. We also received the SOC2 packet — thanks for that.

I'll follow up if the payment doesn't land by 2027-12-03.

Best,
Marie
Head of Finance, Greenleaf Analytics
marie@greenleafanalytics.com

Attachment: greenleaf-20271130-remittance.pdf (application/pdf)
